newsitem.title: FRANCE: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest -June 27.
newsitem.headline: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest -June 27.

text.p: REUTERS FRENCH ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the French press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet and Brand-name Products.
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
CANNES - Publicis chairman Maurice Levy says he is unhappy to learn of talks between U.S. advertising groups Bozell and True North Communications Inc from press reports. (Reuter)

CANNES - Creative teams in French advertising agencies lack inspiration because of France's economic crisis, says Jacques Seguela, vice-chairman of Havas Advertising and a guru of the French advertising industry. (Reuter)
PARIS - Advertising in French men's magazines jumped by 36.4 percent in value terms in the first four months of this year compared with a year earlier, magazine Carat Medias Actualites says. (Reuter)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET

PARIS - French digital satellite television service Television par Satellite (TPS) says it reaches an accord to broadcast Portugal's SIC, the leading Portuguese private terrestrial television channel. (Reuter)

PARIS - Canalsatellite, the satellite TV unit of French pay television firm Canal Plus, will have 400,000 subscribers next week and exceed the 500,000 threshold at the end of the year, cchairman Bruno Delecour says. (Reuter)
PARIS - Pierre Dauzier, chairman of French media group Havas, says the Havas board would not look at proposals to divest from weekly news magazines Le Point and L'Express until September.
(Reuter)
PARIS - French news agency Agence France Presse (AFP), broker Maison Roussin and computer company Skyworld launch an Internet service to provide real-time financial information. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

GENEVA - The Americans hurt the French by criticising French cheese. The United States angers the European Union with its demands for pasteurisation of dairy products at a meeting of the U.N. body which sets international food safety standards. (Reuter)

MADRID - A planned merger between Spanish sugar producers Ebro de Agricolas and Azucarera will be delayed by a proposal from the governing Popular Party (PP), sources at Ebro say. The PP wants the new group's structure to be Spanish and to guarantee its future, but France's Saint-Louis's Generale Sucriere, a stakeholder in both companies, wants to control the new group. (Reuter)
Paris Editorial, Sue Landau
